giants.title: Giants — The Forbidden Offspring
giants.intro: Born of Watcher and human unions, giants terrorize the earth.

entries.name: Ohya, Son of Semyaza
entries.description: The wrathful first-born of Semyaza. Plagued by nightmares of the coming deluge.

academicDossier.scholarlySynthesis: Ohya is the wrathful first-born son of the Watcher Semyaza and a human woman, representing the first generation of Nephilim titans.
academicDossier.anthropologicalInsights: Ohya's character reflects the 'monstrous hybridity' that necessitates the Flood. Anthropologically, he symbolizes the existential dread of a being that violates cosmic boundaries, representing the doomed legacy of the Grigori whose rebellion at Mt. Hermon fractured the natural order.
academicDossier.mythicalBeliefs: According to the Book of Giants, Ohya was plagued by nightmares of the coming Deluge and sought the prophet Enoch to interpret his visions of doom.

entries.name: Hahya, Brother of Ohya
entries.description: The contemplative brother who dreamt of the garden where only one tree remained.

academicDossier.scholarlySynthesis: Hahya is the contemplative brother of Ohya and son of the Watcher Semyaza, noted for his prophetic sensitivity and visions.
academicDossier.anthropologicalInsights: Hahya serves as a symbol of the internal conflict and prophetic dread within the giant lineages. His contemplative nature highlights the tension between their celestial origin as sons of Egregores and their terrestrial fate.
academicDossier.mythicalBeliefs: Hahya famously dreamt of a garden being submerged where only one tree with three branches remained, which was interpreted as the survival of Noah and his sons.

entries.name: Mahway, the Winged
entries.description: Son of Barakel. The messenger sent to find Enoch at the ends of the earth.

academicDossier.scholarlySynthesis: Mahway is a winged giant and the son of the Watcher Barakel, distinguished by his ability for true flight and his role as a celestial messenger.
academicDossier.anthropologicalInsights: Mahway represents the role of the intermediary. As a winged Grigori-hybrid, he bridges the gap between the corrupted urban-imperial cultures and the nomadic prophetic line of Enoch, carrying the plea of the hybrid legacy before the divine 'police force'.
academicDossier.mythicalBeliefs: Tradition holds that Mahway flew to the ends of the earth to find Enoch, carrying the plea of the Nephilim for intercession before the Most High.

entries.name: Gilgamesh
entries.description: A giant mentioned in the Dead Sea Scrolls, confused by the nightmares of his brethren.

academicDossier.scholarlySynthesis: Gilgamesh is a legendary figure of immense strength, integrated into the Enochic narrative through a process of syncretism where he is explicitly identified as a Nephilim or Giant in the Dead Sea Scrolls.
academicDossier.anthropologicalInsights: The inclusion of Gilgamesh reflects the polemic clash between nomadic Jewish culture and the decadent urban-imperial cultures of Babylon. By identifying the great Sumerian king as a monstrous hybrid destined for judgment, the text subverts the heroic ideals of the Mesopotamian empire.
academicDossier.mythicalBeliefs: In the Book of Giants found among the Dead Sea Scrolls, Gilgamesh is a 'wrestler supreme' who is deeply troubled and confused by the prophetic nightmares of his brethren regarding the coming Flood.

corrupted.title: Corrupted Humanity
corrupted.intro: Those who have turned from the Creator to serve the Nephilim.

entries.name: Baal-Priest
entries.description: Priests who perform blood sacrifices to fuel dark miracles.

academicDossier.scholarlySynthesis: Baal-Priests are human servitors who have abandoned the worship of the Creator to serve the Nephilim and their fallen angelic patrons.
academicDossier.anthropologicalInsights: These priests represent the institutionalization of corruption, where human religious structures are co-opted to maintain the dominance of giant overlords.
academicDossier.mythicalBeliefs: They are believed to perform blood sacrifices and dark rituals to channel demonic power, effectively acting as the spiritual enforcers of the Watchers' legacy.

entries.name: Lamech the Avenger
entries.description: The Cainite king who boasted of killing a man for wounding him.

academicDossier.scholarlySynthesis: Lamech the Avenger is a Cainite king who personifies the extreme escalation of violence and pride in the antediluvian world.
academicDossier.anthropologicalInsights: Lamech represents the 'seventy-sevenfold' escalation of the mark of Cain, symbolizing a society where personal vengeance has replaced divine law.
academicDossier.mythicalBeliefs: His boast to his wives, Adah and Zillah, about killing a man for a mere wound is seen as the narrative climax of human depravity before the Flood.
